subject: Tokens/sec warranty, measurement plan, and discount tiers
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Tokens/sec warranty, measurement plan, and discount tiers

Hi Lydia —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m putting a concise proposal on the table for how Redwood would approach dedicated GPU pool sizing, an objective tokens/sec (TPS) warranty, and a simple discount band structure tied to committed throughput.

High-level proposal:
- Baseline commit: 500k tokens/sec sustained across the reserved pool (measured as aggregate tokens generated per second over 5-minute windows).
- Warranty bands (monthly SLA credits):
  * Band A (>=95% of committed TPS): 0% credit
  * Band B (90–95%): 10% monthly credit
  * Band C (<90%): 25% monthly credit (escalation triggers)
- Latency targets: 95th percentile tail latency for single-request median prompt (512 tokens) <= 400ms at baseline commit levels; requests/sec goals are a soft proxy and we measure primary by tokens/sec.

Measurement methodology (draft):
- Measurement windows: 5-minute sliding windows, reported hourly and aggregated for monthly SLOs.
- Test harness: continuous synthetic load (mix of short and long prompts matching your traffic profile) + customer sampling (we can run opt-in production probes with masked customer data).
- Discount trigger: credit calculated against total monthly invoice if aggregate monthly measured TPS falls into lower bands. Credits are capped at 50% of monthly committed spend.

I’ve attached a short pricing worksheet (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf) and a one-page test outline. Quick asks: can you confirm the expected request size distribution (tokens per request) and whether Acme needs per-customer isolation or aggregate pool is acceptable?

If that looks reasonable I can loop Karthik in with a technical measurement appendix and a short canary plan for onboarding.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Lydia Chang <lydia@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 11:04:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Tokens/sec warranty, measurement plan, and discount tiers

Markus —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side before we escalate to procurement:

1) Token definition: do you count generated tokens only or input+output? For our billing model we need generated + consumed because prompts are sizeable.
2) Measurement windows: if we have bursty traffic (many short spikes), how does that affect the 5-minute sliding window calculation? We’re worried short bursts will be smoothed out and not reflect customer-facing latency impact.
3) Isolation: Acme prefers logical isolation by customer in the near term (we have regulatory tenants) — would that require a dedicated sub-pool and change pricing materially?

Also, procurement asked for example contract language describing the credit calculation and any test-execution responsibilities on Acme’s side (e.g., test accounts, traffic mirroring).

If you can send a short appendix addressing 1–3 we can get the PO side engaged.

—Lydia
VP Product, Acme Analytics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia@acmeanalytics.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 08:22:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Tokens/sec warranty, measurement plan, and discount tiers

Thanks Lydia — quick responses inline.

On Tue, Mar 2, 2027 at 11:04 AM Lydia Chang <lydia@acmeanalytics.com> wrote:
> 1) Token definition: do you count generated tokens only or input+output?

We measure tokens as input + output for the TPS warranty. Reason: overall GPU work correlates with sum of input+output tokens (KV cache and attention compute). The pricing worksheet assumes generated+consumed tokens. We’ll call it T_total in the contract text.

> 2) Measurement windows: if we have bursty traffic (many short spikes), how does that affect the 5-minute sliding window calculation?

The 5-minute sliding window is intentionally conservative — it captures sustained throughput and prevents overfitting to nano-bursts. For latency-sensitive customer-facing concerns, we recommend a secondary latency SLO (95th pct tail as Markus noted) that is measured per-request at the frontdoor. If you need per-customer latency guarantees we can layer that but it increases isolation complexity.

> 3) Isolation: Acme prefers logical isolation by customer — would that require a dedicated sub-pool and change pricing materially?

Logical isolation (namespaces + scheduling priority) is feasible in our Dedicated product and typically adds ~15–25% premium over aggregate pools depending on sizing. Fully physical isolation (separate GPU hosts) is more expensive (~50%+). We can provide a sizing delta estimate once you share expected active tenants and peak concurrency per tenant.

Measurement appendix (short):
- Primary metric: aggregate T_total per 5-minute window across the reserved pool.
- Secondary metrics: 95p tail latency (per-request) at 512-token median, 99p for critical endpoints.
- Test mechanics: Redwood runs controlled synthetic tests during mutually agreed maintenance windows; Acme can opt to provide mirrored traffic via a test API key for production-shaped samples.
- Evidence: we publish hourly measurement logs and a monthly SLA report; credits are calculated automatically by our billing pipeline.

I’ll attach a CSV test template (SLA-test-plan.csv) and a sample contract clause next mail.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Tokens/sec warranty, measurement plan, and discount tiers

Lydia —

Great, thanks for the quick review. Based on Karthik’s notes and your asks, here’s a compact mutual action plan to surface to procurement:

MVP SLA + commercial ask (summary):
1) Commit: 500k T_total TPS (input+output) aggregate, measured as 5-minute sliding windows; monthly aggregation determines band.
2) Latency: 95p <= 400ms at baseline for 512-token median requests; 99p reported for critical endpoints.
3) Discount bands: 0% / 10% / 25% credits as previously described; credits capped at 50% of committed monthly spend.
4) Isolation: logical isolation available at +20% premium; physical isolation quoted separately.
5) Onboarding: 2-week canary run (mutually scheduled) followed by a 4-week ramp to full commit. During canary Redwood will run the synthetic tests; Acme may optionally enable mirrored traffic.
6) Documentation: Redwood will provide a measurement appendix, CSV test template (attached), and a contract clause draft for procurement.

Next steps: If this summary is acceptable I’ll: (a) update the pricing worksheet with the +20% logical isolation scenario, (b) produce the 1-page contract clause, and (c) share a DocuSign envelope for a statement of work covering the canary dates.

Please confirm the ramp dates window that works for your team next week and whether procurement needs any additional artifacts.

Thanks,
Markus
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
